description: Supplier quality view for the gateway, externally shareable: outcomes only. Scoped to mainnet and client traffic. No template variables: Grafana public dashboards do not support them.

options.content:
# Gateway — public pinned view
**Scope:** mainnet, client traffic (`request_type=client`) unless a panel says otherwise. Operators are registrable domains. No filters: public dashboards do not support variables.

panels.description: Client requests to the gateway: one per request, whatever retries, hedges or batch items it fanned out into.
panels.title: Incoming RPS

panels.description: Upstream relay attempts for client traffic: every retry, hedge arm and batch item counts. Probes excluded.
panels.title: Outgoing Relays/s

panels.description: Live WebSocket bridges: a client connection plus its supplier connection.
panels.title: Active WebSockets

panels.description: First client attempts whose outcome the heuristic did not blame on the supplier: a good answer, or a chain or client error the supplier answered honestly (block not found, execution reverted). First attempts only: retries arrive after another host failed, with less time left.
panels.title: Relay Success %

panels.description: Median upstream attempt latency, client traffic. Client-facing latency is in the Latency row.
panels.title: Relay Latency P50

panels.description: Share of client requests the gateway answered with a 5xx: what clients actually saw, after retries and hedges. A node's own 5xx answer (CometBFT's HTTP 500 for an unknown tx) is the chain answering and is left out.
panels.title: Client 5xx %

panels.description: Client requests by the status class the gateway answered, last 24h.
panels.title: Requests in 24H

panels.description: Client requests by status class over the dashboard time range.
panels.title: Requests in range

panels.description: Upstream client relay attempts by the HTTP status class the relay miner returned, last 24h. The exact codes are in the Relays by Status Code panel.
panels.title: Relays in 24H

panels.description: Upstream client relay attempts by status class over the dashboard time range.
panels.title: Relays in range
Supplier Quality (Operator / Service / RPC type) — client traffic

panels.description: Per operator (registrable domain), service and RPC type, client attempts only. RPS and latency count every attempt; Success % and Supplier err/s count first attempts only (the fair sample: retries arrive with less time left after another host failed). Success % counts a good answer and a chain or client error the supplier answered honestly; only supplier and unknown attributions count against it. Latency is per attempt. Session eps is the operator's registrations in the current session.
panels.title: HTTP Supplier Quality — excludes WebSocket

targets.expr: (1 - (sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution=~"supplier|unknown"}) or sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first"}) * 0) / (sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first"}) > 0)) * 100
sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution=~"supplier|unknown"})
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type, le) (sage:operator_attempt_seconds_bucket:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage"})) * 1000
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type, le) (sage:operator_attempt_seconds_bucket:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage"})) * 1000
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type, le) (sage:operator_attempt_seconds_bucket:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage"})) * 1000
max by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage_session_endpoints{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", rpc_type!="websocket"})

panels.description: First client attempts (the fair sample) by the side the heuristic blamed. supplier: the relay miner or node failed (5xx, 408, timeouts, bad answers). unknown: failed with no verdict either way. chain: the node answered honestly about chain state (block not found, pruned history) — never penalised. client: the request's own fault (invalid params, execution reverted) — never penalised. Only supplier and unknown count as fault.
panels.title: Error Attribution by Operator — what's dragging Success %

targets.expr: sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution="supplier"})
sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution="unknown"})
sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution="blockchain"})
sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution="client"})

sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first", attribution=~"supplier|unknown"}) / (sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage:operator_attempts:rate4m{environment="mainnet-sage", attempt="first"}) > 0) * 100

panels.description: Where each operator's registrations in the current session stand with the gateway: in rotation (all selectable at full weight), partly demoted (some of them sent less traffic after failures), demoted (all of them), drained (removed from the service's pool for now). The Failure Reasons table beside it says why.
panels.title: Operator Status (HTTP)

targets.expr: (max by (service_id, operator) (label_replace(sage_drained_operators{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}, "operator", "$1", "domain", "(.*)")) > 0) * 0 + 4 or ((sum by (service_id, operator) (max by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage_session_endpoints_low{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", rpc_type!="websocket"})) >= sum by (service_id, operator) (max by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage_session_endpoints{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", rpc_type!="websocket"}))) and (sum by (service_id, operator) (max by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage_session_endpoints{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", rpc_type!="websocket"})) > 0)) * 0 + 3 or (sum by (service_id, operator) (max by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage_session_endpoints_low{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", rpc_type!="websocket"})) > 0) * 0 + 2 or (sum by (service_id, operator) (max by (service_id, operator, rpc_type) (sage_session_endpoints{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", rpc_type!="websocket"})) > 0) * 0 + 1

panels.description: What the gateway recorded against each operator in the last hour, client traffic and health checks: transport_timeout (accepted the connection, no answer in time), http_5xx / upstream_5xx (the backend or the relay miner failed), stale_response (answered with a chain head behind), html_response (an error page), ws_probe_dial_failed (the WebSocket upgrade failed), ws_endpoint_lost (a live WebSocket dropped), and the like. Only failures the gateway blames on the supplier's side are counted.
panels.title: Failure Reasons by Operator (last 1h)

targets.expr: sum by (service_id, operator, rpc_type, reason) (increase(sage_operator_failures_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h])) > 0

panels.description: By the RPC type the gateway settled on for the request (header or detection).
panels.title: Client Requests by RPC Type

panels.description: Every client attempt by whose fault its outcome was; none = a good answer.
panels.title: Attempt Attribution

panels.description: What the client waited, retries and hedges included: from the request reaching the gateway to the response written.
panels.title: Client-Facing Latency Percentiles

panels.description: Requests that ran out of their deadline. The error log names the operators in flight for each one ("attempts" and the hedge deadline message).
panels.title: Client 504s by Service

panels.description: What clients saw, per service. A service high here with a clean supplier table usually lacks a supplier that can serve its requests at all (archival state, an RPC type nobody stakes).
panels.title: Worst Services (client 5xx)

targets.expr: sum by (service_id) (rate(sage_client_requests_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", status=~"5..", origin!="chain"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (service_id) (rate(sage_client_requests_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[$__rate_interval])) * 100 > 0

panels.description: Bridges ended, by who ended them. gateway closes are the gateway's own decision (a deadline, a rebind that found nowhere to go); client and endpoint closes are the peers'.
panels.title: WebSocket Closes by Initiator

panels.description: How long one supplier served one client connection, bind to rebind or close. A connection that rebinds is several tenures, so this is a lower bound on connection lifetime.
panels.title: Supplier Tenure per Connection (p50/p90/p99)

panels.description: ok: for a subscription open on the connection. duplicate: a byte-for-byte repeat of one of the last 8. unsolicited: for a subscription never opened with that supplier. Both are relays nobody asked for.
panels.title: Subscription Notifications by Grade

panels.description: Per operator and service. Every frame in either direction is a relay the supplier can claim, and the push rate on a subscription is chosen by the supplier being paid, so Frames /conn is worth comparing across operators on the same service. Dup+unsolicited % is notifications nobody asked for. Frame columns show only while the operator holds a live connection. WS session eps is the operator's registrations in the session.
panels.title: WebSocket Supplier Quality by Operator/Service

targets.expr: sum by (service_id, operator) (rate(sage_websocket_supplier_frames_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", direction="endpoint_to_client"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (service_id, operator) (sum by (service_id, operator) (sage_websocket_supplier_connections{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}) > 0)

sum by (service_id, operator) (rate(sage_websocket_supplier_frames_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", direction="client_to_endpoint"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (service_id, operator) (sum by (service_id, operator) (sage_websocket_supplier_connections{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}) > 0)

sum by (service_id, operator) (rate(sage_websocket_supplier_notifications_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage", grade=~"duplicate|unsolicited"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (service_id, operator) (rate(sage_websocket_supplier_notifications_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[$__rate_interval])) * 100
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (service_id, operator, le) (rate(sage_websocket_supplier_tenure_seconds_bucket{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h]))) >= 0

panels.description: Blast radius: the largest operator's share of each service over the last hour. High share means one operator failing takes most of the service with it. Share only; no operator named.
panels.title: Supplier Concentration — top operator share per service (HTTP + WS)

targets.expr: ( max by (service_id) (sum by (service_id, operator) (rate(sage_operator_attempts_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h]))) / on (service_id) sum by (service_id) (rate(sage_operator_attempts_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h])) ) and on (service_id) (sum by (service_id) (rate(sage_operator_attempts_total{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h])) > 0)

( max by (service_id) (sum by (service_id, operator) (avg_over_time(sage_websocket_supplier_connections{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h]))) / on (service_id) sum by (service_id) (avg_over_time(sage_websocket_supplier_connections{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h])) ) and on (service_id) (sum by (service_id) (avg_over_time(sage_websocket_supplier_connections{job="sage", environment="mainnet-sage"}[1h])) > 0)
